Computing Without Computers

Drawing becomes a way to think through instructions, conditions and external inputs. Across three analog studies, students examine artworks, execute established systems, then author new works for other people to realize.

  1. Week 03Instruction, Execution, and Iteration
  2. Week 04Conditions, Shared State, and Emergence
  3. Week 05Chance, Data, and Participation

01

Lecture

Read artworks as systems: identify the instruction, decisions and relationships that organize a result.

02

Lab

Execute a classic artwork or a clearly identified classroom adaptation through paper, tools and human judgment.

03

Exercise

Design an original work using related principles. Test a written score and let other people’s actions enter the result.

WEEK 03

Instruction, Execution, and Iteration

A drawing instruction separates the idea from its execution. Repetition, interpretation and small differences allow one rule to produce a family of situated results.

WEEK 04

Conditions, Shared State, and Emergence

A group can produce a coherent drawing by responding to the same changing page. Roles, local conditions and turn-taking organize a result that no participant plans in advance.

WEEK 05

Chance, Data, and Participation

An instruction can receive inputs the artist does not fully control. A chance event, a recorded value or another person’s contribution enters through a designed rule and leaves a visible trace.

About the studies

Three weeks of VIS104 / Digital Design I, taught by Aven-Le Zhou. The sequence connects instruction and iteration, conditional group drawing, and chance, data and participation.

The work happens with paper, drawing tools and people. Each week separates the lecture, execution of an existing work, and authorship of a new student work.

Images show historical reference works discussed in class. Classroom activities are identified as studies or adaptations. Artwork records and image providers remain credited beside the images.
